## Questions and answers
### Do you only work with clients in Brampton?
No. I'm based in Brampton but work remotely, by phone and video, with clients anywhere in Ontario. Documents are signed electronically, so you never need to come to an office.

### What languages do you speak?
English, Gujarati and Hindi. Use whichever you are most comfortable with.

### What is an alternative lender?
A federally or provincially regulated lender, like a trust company or credit union, that takes on files the big banks decline. (In the industry they are sometimes called B-lenders.) Rates are higher, but the path to ownership is real.

### How are alternative lender rates different?
Typically 1–3% higher than the big banks' rates, plus a lender fee. I'm transparent about this upfront — there are no surprises on closing day.

### Will applying hurt my credit score?
A single mortgage application is one hard inquiry — minimal impact. I do a soft pull first before we go anywhere near a formal application.

### My bank won't renew my mortgage. What now?
You still have options. Your current lender may renew once any missed payments are caught up. If not, an alternative lender can often take the mortgage over, and a short private mortgage can bridge the gap while your credit recovers. Start about four months before your renewal date.

### What happens when my term is up?
I reach out a few months before your renewal, compare your options, and tell you plainly whether to stay or switch.

### What documents do I need?
Depends on your situation — but typically ID, 3–6 months of bank statements, proof of income (T4, NOA, or business financials), and a property address. I'll give you a specific list on our first call.

### What are your fees?
I'm paid by the lender on most deals. On some private/B files there's a brokerage fee — I'll tell you the exact number before you commit to anything.

### What is a private mortgage?
A short-term loan, usually one to two years, from a private lender or mortgage investment company. It's approved mainly on your property's equity rather than your income or credit. It costs more than an alternative lender, so I use it as a bridge: solve the problem now, then set you up with something longer-term.

## Alternative mortgages in Ontario
A bank decline isn't the end of the road. Alternative lenders are regulated trust companies and credit unions that look at the files the big banks turn away, and they're where most of my clients start.
- Is an alternative lender safe? Yes. Alternative lenders are regulated lenders, not loan sharks. Your mortgage is a normal registered mortgage with a set term and set payments. The difference is the rate and the approval rules.
- How much down payment does an alternative lender need? Usually 20% for a purchase, because most alternative mortgages are uninsured. On a refinance you can typically borrow up to about 80% of your home’s value.
- Will an alternative mortgage hurt my credit? No. It is a normal mortgage, and paying it on time strengthens your credit file like any other.
- How fast can an alternative lender approve a mortgage? Once the file is complete, a decision often comes within a few business days. The full timeline depends on the appraisal, conditions and your closing date, so start as early as you can.
- Can I use an alternative lender to renew or refinance, not just to buy? Yes. Alternative lenders handle purchases, refinances and switches at renewal. Renewal is often when people discover their bank won't keep them, and an alternative lender can be the answer.

## Mortgages for buying a home
A first mortgage is the main loan on the home you buy. I shop it across lenders, get you pre-approved, and stay on the file until you have the keys.
- How long does a pre-approval last? Most lenders hold the rate for 90 to 120 days. If you have not bought by then, we renew it at whatever rate applies at the time.
- Is a pre-approval a guarantee? No. The lender still has to approve the property itself and confirm your documents. It does tell you what you can realistically spend.
- Fixed or variable? It depends on how much payment movement you can live with and how long you plan to keep the home. I lay out both side by side before you choose.
- How much should I budget for closing costs? A common rule of thumb is about 1.5% to 4% of the purchase price, on top of your down payment. Land transfer tax is usually the biggest piece. I'll give you an estimate for your price range before you make offers.
- Should I get pre-approved before I start looking? Yes. It tells you your real budget, holds a rate while you shop, and shows sellers you're serious. It also surfaces any problems early, while there's time to fix them.

## Mortgage refinancing
Refinancing replaces your mortgage with a new one, usually to lower your payments, pay off high-interest debt, or take equity out of your home. I'll show you whether the savings beat the cost before you decide.
- How much does it cost to refinance? Expect a legal fee, usually an appraisal, and a penalty if you're mid-term. I lay out the full cost next to the savings so you can see whether it's worth it.
- Can I refinance with bad credit? Often, yes, through an alternative lender or a private lender, as long as you have enough equity in your home.
- Should I refinance now or wait for my renewal? If your renewal is close, making changes at renewal avoids a penalty. If it's far off and you're carrying high-interest debt, refinancing now can still save money. It comes down to the numbers.
- Will checking my options hurt my credit? No. I start with a soft check, which does not affect your score. A full credit check only happens when you decide to apply.

## Home equity line of credit (HELOC)
A HELOC is a line of credit secured by your home. You borrow what you need, when you need it, and pay interest only on what you've used.
- Who qualifies for a HELOC? HELOCs are mostly offered by the big banks and other prime lenders, so they need good credit and provable income. If that is not you yet, a second mortgage may fit better.
- Is the rate fixed? Usually not. Most HELOCs are variable, tied to the lender’s prime rate, so the cost moves with interest rates.
- Can I add a HELOC when I renew? Often, yes. Renewal is a good time to set one up because you're already reviewing the mortgage.
- Is a HELOC better than a second mortgage? It depends. A HELOC is usually cheaper and more flexible, but needs good credit and provable income. A second mortgage is easier to qualify for, especially with bruised credit, but costs more. I'll tell you which one you can actually get.
- Can the lender reduce my HELOC limit? Yes. Most credit lines can be reviewed, reduced or called in by the lender. That's rare, but it's why a HELOC shouldn't be your only plan for money you'll definitely need.

## Mortgage renewal
When your term ends, your lender sends a renewal offer, and many people simply sign it. It's the one time you can move without a penalty, so it's worth a second look.
- Do I have to pass the stress test to switch lenders at renewal? Usually not, if you're keeping the same amount and amortization. That rule changed in late 2024. Borrowing more at renewal is treated differently.
- Does switching lenders cost anything? Often very little: many lenders cover the legal and appraisal costs on a straight switch. I'll confirm the costs for your lender.
- Can I take out equity when I renew? Yes. That's a refinance at renewal, and it's often the cheapest time to do it because there's no penalty to break your term.
- My bank won't renew my mortgage. What can I do? Start by finding out why, and whether getting caught up on payments changes their answer. If it doesn't, an alternative lender can often take over the mortgage, and a short private mortgage can bridge the gap while your credit recovers. The earlier you start, the more options you have.
- Can I renew if I've missed payments? Often, yes. Many lenders will renew once you're caught up, though the rate may be higher. If your current lender won't, alternative lenders look at the whole picture rather than just the missed payments.
- What happens if my term ends and I haven't signed anything? Lenders handle this differently. Some move you into a short or open term at a higher rate, and some send a demand. Don't let it lapse: start comparing about four months before your renewal date.

## Private mortgages and private lending
When even an alternative lender can't help in time, a private mortgage can. It's short-term money secured by your property's equity, used to fix a problem now and set up something better next.
- How long does a private mortgage last? Usually one year, sometimes two. Payments are often interest-only. The point is to give you time to fix the problem, then move to a cheaper lender.
- Can I get a private mortgage with bad credit? Often, yes, if there is enough equity in the property. Private lenders care most about the equity and the plan to repay.
- What is a private second mortgage? A loan registered behind your existing mortgage. You keep your current mortgage and its rate, and borrow against the equity on top of it.
- How fast can a private mortgage close? Often within days to a couple of weeks, once the appraisal and lawyers are ready. Speed is one of the main reasons people use private money.
- Is private lending legal and regulated? Yes, when it's done properly. In Ontario, private mortgages are arranged by licensed mortgage agents and brokers, registered on title, and closed through lawyers. Avoid anyone who skips those steps.

## Second mortgages
A second mortgage lets you borrow against your home without touching the mortgage you already have. You keep your current rate on the first.
- Do I need good credit for a second mortgage? Not always. Many second mortgages come from alternative lenders or private lenders who focus on your equity more than your credit score.
- Is a second mortgage the same as a HELOC? Not quite. A second mortgage is usually a lump sum with set payments. A HELOC is a credit line you draw on as needed, and usually needs stronger credit.
- Can I pay it off early? Often, yes, but terms vary. Some private loans charge a fee for early payout. I'll tell you before you sign.
- Will my first mortgage lender find out? A second mortgage is registered on your property's title, so it's on the record. Some first mortgages have terms about additional borrowing, so I check yours before we apply.

## Reverse mortgages for homeowners 55+
A reverse mortgage lets homeowners 55 and older turn part of their home's value into tax-free cash, without monthly mortgage payments and without selling. I'll show you the real costs, and the alternatives, before you decide.
- Is the money taxable? No. It's a loan, not income, so it isn't taxed and generally doesn't affect Old Age Security or the Guaranteed Income Supplement.
- Do I have to make monthly payments? No. You can pay the interest if you want to, but you don't have to. The loan is repaid when the home is sold or you move out.
- Can I lose my home? Not for missing payments, because there are none. You do need to live there, pay your property tax and insurance, and keep the home in good repair. Those are the conditions of the loan.
- Will my family still inherit the home? Your estate keeps whatever equity is left once the loan is repaid. Many families sell the home and keep the difference, or repay the loan and keep the home.
- Can I get one if I still have a mortgage? Often, yes. The existing mortgage is paid off from the reverse mortgage first, which also ends those monthly payments.

## Commercial mortgages
Commercial lending runs on different rules from home mortgages. Lenders look at the property and its income as much as at you, and I find the ones that fit your deal.
- How much down payment do I need for a commercial property? Usually 25% to 35%, depending on the property type and lender. Some multi-unit residential programs allow less.
- How long does commercial financing take? Longer than a home mortgage: appraisals and environmental reports can add weeks. Start early, especially with a firm closing date.
- Can I get a commercial mortgage with a newer business? It's harder but possible, particularly if the property itself has strong income or you have a larger down payment.
- Can I get a commercial mortgage for the building my business operates from? Yes. Owner-occupied commercial property is common. Lenders look at your business's finances alongside the property, and the down payment is usually higher than on a home.
- What's an environmental report, and do I need one? Many commercial lenders ask for a Phase I environmental site assessment, a review of whether past uses could have contaminated the property. Whether you need one depends on the property and the lender. I'll tell you early so it doesn't delay closing.
